item.title: Becerra and Hilton to Face Off in Televised California Governor Debate
item.description: Xavier Becerra, a Democrat who served in the Biden administration, will debate Steve Hilton, a Republican former talk show host, in what’s likely to be their only face-off before the election.
item.dc:creator: Laurel Rosenhall
item.media:description: Xavier Becerra, left, and Steve Hilton will appear in their only scheduled debate on Wednesday night on CNN.

item.title: Judge Ends Federal Oversight of Oakland Police After 23 Years
item.description: In ending the longest such monitoring in U.S. history, a federal court said the department had mostly complied with reforms mandated by a 2003 settlement after a police brutality lawsuit.
item.dc:creator: Yan Zhuang
item.media:description: An Oakland police officer seen in uniform in 2025.

item.title: Ken Paxton, G.O.P. Nominee in Texas, Privately Said Trump’s Convention Hurt Him
item.description: Ken Paxton, one of the party’s top Senate candidates and a Trump loyalist, said that “everybody’s numbers dropped” after the event, according to audio obtained by The Times.
item.dc:creator: Theodore Schleifer
item.media:credit: Shelby Tauber for The New York Times
item.media:description: Ken Paxton, the Republican nominee for Senate in Texas, as President Trump addressed him during the second day of the Republican midterm convention in Dallas this month.

item.title: Donor Gives $3 Billion to Carnegie Mellon, the Largest University Gift Ever
item.description: The donation by Kenneth Griffin, intended mostly to help build a campus in Miami, was the biggest single gift in the history of U.S. higher education.
item.dc:creator: Alan Blinder
item.media:credit: Martina Tuaty for The New York Times
item.media:description: The donation from the hedge fund executive Kenneth C. Griffin is more than the record $2 billion gift given to Oregon Health and Science University recently.

item.title: 55 Swatting Calls: A Couple’s Fight Against Online Stalkers and the Police
item.description: The city of Milwaukee agreed to a $575,000 settlement after months of heavily armed police responses to 911 calls to the couple’s home that officials knew were hoaxes.
item.dc:creator: Adeel Hassan

item.title: ‘It’s Not an Issue’: Crime as a G.O.P. Line of Attack Loses Traction
item.description: Across the country, especially in the North Carolina Senate race, Republicans have charged opponents with being soft on crime, even as crime rates plummet.
item.dc:creator: Shaila Dewan

item.media:description: Roy Cooper, the Democratic candidate for Senate in North Carolina, at a rally in Durham, N.C.

item.title: Hispanic Voters on the Texas Border Have Soured on Trump
item.description: In 2024, these voters were an essential part of the winning Republican coalition. Now, many feel abandoned and furious, complicating the party’s chances in November.
item.dc:creator: Jennifer Medina and Edgar Sandoval
item.media:credit: Tamir Kalifa for The New York Times

item.title: Do Families Have a Right to Hug Their Jailed Loved Ones?
item.description: A growing number of jails allow only virtual calls. Some families are suing for the right to see inmates in person.
item.dc:creator: Tim Arango
item.media:credit: Ulysses Ortega for The New York Times
item.media:description: Joseph Duran Jr. and other people with relatives in jail are suing Solano County, Calif., to restore visitation rights.

item.title: Vying for Undecideds, L.A. Mayor Candidates Talk Affordability and Israel
item.description: Mayor Karen Bass and her onetime ally, Nithya Raman, made their case to voters with just five weeks left until the election.
item.dc:creator: Shawn Hubler

item.title: Former Music Pastor Is Convicted of His Wife’s Murder
item.description: The trial in Ohio attracted outsize attention because the defendant, Caleb Flynn, auditioned on “American Idol” in 2013.
item.dc:creator: Jennifer Sinco Kelleher
item.media:description: Caleb Flynn, a former music pastor who auditioned for “American Idol” in 2013, was found guilty on Tuesday of murdering his wife, Ashley, in February.

item.title: Voice of America Cuts Hurt ‘U.S. National Interests,’ Internal Watchdog Says
item.description: The assessment by the State Department’s inspector general echoes concerns raised by critics of the move to shutter V.O.A., including some Republicans in Congress.
item.dc:creator: Minho Kim
item.media:description: A State Department inspector general’s report found that the Trump administration’s push to shutter Voice of America hurt the U.S. goal of supporting democratic values around the world.

item.title: Air Force Major Recommended for General Court-Martial After Protesting Trump
item.description: The recommendations are not binding, but it is rare for them to be ignored in the military justice system.
item.dc:creator: Anushka Patil

item.title: Who Attended Trump’s AI Luncheon, and Who Sat Where
item.description: A seating chart of the meeting illustrated growing divisions within the artificial intelligence industry and how it is viewed by the White House.
item.dc:creator: Cecilia Kang
item.media:description: Some of the biggest proponents of aggressive regulation were relegated to the far reaches of the table, which sat 34 people at the luncheon.

item.title: Democrats in Congress Embrace a More Punitive Posture Toward Israel
item.description: Nearly every Democratic senator voted to advance a measure calling for a human rights report on Israel’s conduct in the West Bank, as some in the party propose punishing settlement activity with sanctions.
item.dc:creator: Robert Jimison and Annie Karni
item.category: War Crimes, Genocide and Crimes Against Humanity
item.media:description: Palestinian villagers harvesting olives in the village of Turmus Aya, with Israeli settlements in the background, northeast of Ramallah in the occupied West Bank in 2025.

item.title: Cornell’s Chi Phi Chapter Faces Scrutiny Over Assault Accusations
item.description: Chi Phi’s Cornell chapter was shuttered after a woman said its members sexually assaulted her. It was one of the oldest fraternities at the school, where Greek life has thrived.
item.dc:creator: Alan Blinder and Michael S. Schmidt
item.media:credit: Heather Ainsworth for The New York Times
item.media:description: The Chi Phi fraternity house at Cornell University.

item.title: Trump Launches America.gov, an AI Chatbot That Contradicts Some of His Claims
item.description: Democrats amplified statements from America.gov that frequently contradict the president on tariffs, election fraud and other topics.
item.dc:creator: Chris Cameron
item.media:description: The chatbot calls itself “America” and fact-checks many of President Trump’s most common false claims.

item.title: X2, the Troubled California Six Flags Roller Coaster, Reaches Its End
item.description: The ride at Magic Mountain near Los Angeles has fueled lawsuits claiming that it had caused brain injuries, including two that were fatal.
item.dc:creator: Neil Vigdor
item.category: California Division of Occupational Safety and Health
item.media:description: Riders experienced up to four times the force of gravity on X2 at Six Flags Magic Mountain in Valencia, Calif. The ride had attracted criticism and lawsuits claiming it caused severe injuries.

item.title: University of Michigan Halts New Grading Plan After Backlash From Critics
item.description: The program was intended to address what the university called a “mental health crisis.” But the plan was met with criticism that it was coddling students.

item.media:description: The University of Michigan campus in Ann Arbor.

item.title: At A.I. Event, Trump Asks Meta, OpenAI and Microsoft to Make Safety Decisions Themselves
item.description: President Trump’s meetings with tech leaders produced some voluntary safeguards and a commitment to rebrand artificial intelligence as “super intelligence,” the term that Mr. Trump prefers.

item.title: Ohio Woman Sues Hospital After Wrong Leg Is Amputated
item.description: Sharon Jacks, 74, said she went into surgery for the amputation of her lower right leg last year, but her left leg was removed instead. She has accused Selby General Hospital of negligence.
item.dc:creator: Johnny Diaz
item.media:description: Marietta, Ohio, where Sharon Jacks’s lower left leg was amputated instead at Selby General Hospital in September 2025. A lawsuit says she had gone in to have her lower right leg removed.

item.title: A Very American Makeover for the State Department’s ‘Hall of Flags’
item.description: The flags of dozens of countries had hung above the State Department’s main atrium. A red, white and blue change has sparked a debate.
item.dc:creator: Michael Crowley
item.media:description: Many State Department veterans call the changes to the flags an embarrassing symbol of the Trump administration’s showy brand of nationalism.

item.title: Justice Dept. Unlawfully Withheld Grants to Combat Domestic Violence, Judge Rules
item.description: Judge Melissa R. DuBose said the department had placed arbitrary conditions on grants created by the Violence Against Women Act.
item.dc:creator: Zach Montague
item.media:credit: Demetrius Freeman for The New York Times
item.media:description: The Justice Department. One condition imposed by the administration prohibited grantees from “advancing activities or programs in contravention of executive orders.”

item.title: Latino leaders sign a letter asking Trump to protect long-term undocumented immigrants.
item.dc:creator: Jennifer Medina
item.media:description: A vigil for Lorenzo Salgado Araujo, in Houston, last month. The letter signed by Latino leaders laments the killings of Mr. Salgado Araujo, a undocumented immigrant and father of three who had lived in the United States for decades.

item.title: After 37 Years on Death Row, Man Is Freed From Utah Jail

item.dc:creator: Michael Levenson
item.media:description: Douglas Carter walking out of the Utah County Jail on Monday.

item.title: Supreme Court Allows Trump Administration’s Third-Country Deportations, for Now

item.media:description: A victim was allegedly held in an attic in the city of Malden, a suburb of Boston.

item.title: Victor Marx, Colorado Governor Nominee With Sensational Past, Splinters the G.O.P.

item.title: Man Shot by ICE Agent in Austin Is Charged With Assault
item.description: Prosecutors say Wilber Garces Perez struck an agent with his car’s mirror before another agent shot him. The charge reveals the existence of body camera footage of the shooting, though that video has not been released.

item.media:description: Wilber Rafael Garces Perez was working as a food delivery driver when he was shot by a federal immigration agent in Austin, Texas, on Sept. 20.

item.description: At least three people died after the vessel sank in the Mona Passage, a dangerous stretch of sea often traveled by migrants from Haiti and the Dominican Republic.

item.title: What to Know About the Hacking Group ShinyHunters and Its F.B.I. Breach
item.description: The bureau was the latest target of the notorious gang of cybercriminals that steals sensitive personal data and sells it online.
item.dc:creator: Chris Cameron
item.media:credit: Tierney L. Cross/The New York Times
item.media:description: The information of potentially tens of thousands of former and current F.B.I. employees may have been compromised in a breach by the criminal hacking group known as ShinyHunters.

item.title: Anthropic’s Quest for Humanlike A.I.
item.description: Elizabeth Dias, our national religion correspondent, and Cade Metz, one of our technology reporters, discuss Anthropic’s approach for instilling morality into Claude — which has involved consultations with religious leaders, including ones at the Vatican — and why it’s raising questions.
item.dc:creator: Elizabeth Dias, Cade Metz, Christina Shaman, Chris Whitworth, Stephanie Swart, Whitney Shefte and Mark Oltmanns

item.title: F.B.I. Vows to Pursue ShinyHunters Hackers After Personnel Data Theft
item.description: “We know how to find you,” Brett Leatherman, a senior cyber official at the F.B.I., said in a video statement released Tuesday.
item.dc:creator: Dustin Volz
item.media:description: In a social media post on Tuesday, the F.B.I.’s director, Kash Patel, said the bureau was pursuing leads after an arrest of a person believed to have ties to ShinyHunters.

item.title: ICE Plans 5,000 New Hires to Help With Deportation Drive
item.description: A similar surge last year resulted in undervetted officers initially being let in and then removed as the agency skipped basic checks for new recruits.
item.dc:creator: Alexandra Berzon and Hamed Aleaziz
item.media:description: Immigration and Customs Enforcement in Newark, N.J. in May. The agency has staffed up drastically since President Trump took office, growing by about 8,000, to reach 29,000 employees as of July, according to federal data.

item.title: Trump’s Push for AI Data Center Expansion Puts Some Republican Lawmakers in a Bind
item.description: Some Republicans in close races have distanced themselves from President Trump’s effort to speed the construction of A.I. data centers, citing concerns about rising electricity bills.
item.dc:creator: John Yoon
item.media:credit: Caroline Gutman for The New York Times
item.media:description: A data center under construction in Ashburn, Va., in June. Surveys show that most Americans oppose the construction of data centers to support artificial intelligence.

item.title: Is Claude Conscious? Inside Anthropic’s Quest to Instill Morality Into Its A.I. Models
item.description: In a series of private meetings, the company consulted religious scholars to help instill morality into its A.I. models — and make the case that Claude could be conscious.
item.dc:creator: Elizabeth Dias
item.media:credit: Alessandro Penso for The New York Times
item.media:description: “To be clear,” Christopher Olah told me, “we don’t know if A.I. models are conscious. I don’t know. I’m genuinely uncertain. The thing that I care about is that we get to the right answer, whatever it is.”
